summary: Per-tenant gradual demotion preflight and safety handoff for optimizer profiles (batching/caching/quantization)
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightHealth AI reports unpredictable tail-latency spikes and occasional 5xx errors after applying a combined optimizer profile (aggressive async batching + KV-prefetch + per-layer quantization). They want guidance on a controlled, per-tenant demotion plan that avoids wholesale rollback and preserves capacity while restoring SLOs.

Impact: Intermittent increased 95p/99p latency for several mission-critical endpoints; error rate rose from 0.2% to ~1.8% during peak. Customer is on Dedicated plan with reserved capacity in us-east. Business impact: delayed user responses in production workflows; customer is requesting an SLA-safe mitigation within 48 hours.

Environment: prod, dedicated pool: bh-ai-pool-1, region: us-east, model pinned: open-7b-v1-q4a (tenant override present), runtime version: 2026.02.11, optimizer stack: async-batching:v3 + kv-prefetch:v2 + quant-profile:per-layer-mixed.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a mix of short- and long-sequence requests matching tenant's traffic profile (50% chat, 30% summarization, 20% embeddings) to tenant route /v1/tenants/bha/api/generate. 2) Observe 95p/99p latency spikes after traffic churn and cache-eviction windows. 3) Occasionally observe 503 from an allocator when KV-prefetch eviction collides with async-batch flush.

Logs / traces: Linked Grafana dashboard and sampled traces in comments. Key observation: tail spikes correlate with large mixed-sequence batches and concurrent KV-prefetch eviction events.

Requested outcome: A stepwise per-tenant demotion (soft-landing) plan that: - is safe to run live without full rollback, - preserves most throughput, - allows phased re-enable with gating metrics, - includes preflight checks and a clear handoff to SRE if manual rollback is required.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:21 - Avery Chen: Customer reported tail latency/503 spike after opt profile push. Provided initial data and asked for safe demotion checklist. Marking as P1 due to SLA risk.

2026-03-10 10:04 - Jordan Patel: Reproduced on staging with similar traffic; hypothesizing contention between async batching window and KV eviction causing transient allocator errors. Suggested creating a per-tenant 'soft-demote' traffic-split and temporary batch-size cap as first step.

2026-03-10 13:42 - SRE Oncall (Maya Rivera): Requested exact tenant pool and pool occupancy stats. Pulled allocator and pod logs; saw 503s with message 'kv_eviction_in_progress, allocator busy'. Attached grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/opt/tenant-bh-ai?orgId=1

2026-03-11 08:15 - Support Engineer (Jordan Patel): Outlined preflight checks to customer and proposed stepwise plan (see investigation_notes). Customer approved running a non-disruptive 'shadow demote' to verify no accuracy regressions.

2026-03-12 22:57 - Customer (BrightHealth AI - infra team): Ran shadow traffic for 4 hours; saw 0.4% error rate and minimal accuracy delta on eval set. Requested go-ahead for phased traffic gate tomorrow morning US peak.

2026-03-13 09:02 - Jordan Patel: Executing phase 1 of soft-demote: applied per-tenant batch cap and reduced KV-prefetch window by 30%. Monitoring rules set and notified SRE to be standing by for escalation.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Large async batches are extending enqueue time and overlapping with KV-prefetch eviction triggers, creating resource contention leading to allocator 503s.
Hypothesis 2: Per-layer mixed quantization increases CPU/GPU kernel variability for some sequence lengths, increasing variance under mixed workloads (contributes to tail latency).
Telemetry: 95p latency correlates with two signals: batch_size spikes and concurrent kv_eviction_count > 2. See trace sample: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/0a4f3b

Staging reproduction steps: Use tenant traffic generator (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/tenant-loadgen) with mixed sequence lengths 16/128/1024 distribution. Observed same 503 signature after simulated cache churn.

Preflight checklist performed: 1) Snapshot tenant optimizer config 2) Exported per-route token histograms 3) Validated eval prompt set for accuracy before demote 4) Captured current autoscale and allocator state
Decision: Proceed with 'Soft-demote' approach (per-tenant limited demote) rather than full rollback. This uses traffic-split + config overrides + gating metrics to re-enable parts gradually.
resolution: Workaround applied (phase 1): Per-tenant temporary overrides: async-batching max_window reduced by 30%, batch_size cap set to 64, kv-prefetch window set to conservative mode. Result: 95p latency reduced ~45% in first 2 hours and allocator 503s stopped.

Phase 2 (in progress): Gradual reallocation via traffic-split: 90% traffic to demoted profile, 10% to original for quality checks. Monitor gating metrics: 95p latency, 99p latency, error_rate, model_accuracy_delta. If gating thresholds breached, automatically shift back to 100% demoted profile.

Permanent fix plan: Team will iterate on tuned async-batching heuristics and update KV-prefetch eviction backpressure logic (linked PR above). Long-term: add a per-tenant preflight simulator to validate combined optimizer stacks under realistic token distribution before rollout.

Follow-ups: 1) Postmortem and runbook update scheduled (owner: Jordan Patel) 2) Add tenant-specific circuit-breaker thresholds for KV eviction events 3) Create a console UI quick-action to run 'soft-demote' and snapshot profiles for dedicated tenants.
Status: Monitoring continues; SRE standing by. Customer notified and engaged in phased plan.
